issues.title: Linear-in-time coherence requires a contraction
issues.failure_explanation: From the residual condition, telescoping gives an upper bound of epsilon times the sum of ||K||^j |lambda|^(n-1-j), not a bound uniformly proportional to n epsilon. The old annulus lemma supplies eigenvalues mu with |mu|>1. For a normalized mu-eigenfunction and lambda=mu+epsilon, the residual equals epsilon while |mu^n-(mu+epsilon)^n| grows like n|mu|^(n-1)epsilon, contradicting the claimed linear-in-n estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed approximate temporal coherence is false for the paper's general bounded-operator setting, although the spectral-computation theorems do not rely on this auxiliary assertion.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the unconditional linear-in-time estimate by the telescoping bound ||K_F^n g−λ^n g|| ≤ ε Σ_{j=0}^{n−1} ||K_F||^j |λ|^(n−1−j), and state the bound nε only under an explicit condition such as max{||K_F||,|λ|}≤1. The accompanying coherence discussion must acknowledge the corresponding growth factor outside that regime. No downstream formal result needs alteration because none depends on this assertion.
issues.why_classification: This is not a transcription error: the old source includes expanding eigenvalues, so contraction is not implicit. The exact telescoping estimate gives a local, complete repair and leaves a recognizably comparable coherence statement, but the general linear-in-time rate is substantively weakened in a natural advertised growth regime. That limited rate loss exceeds minor severity without requiring global reconstruction.

issues.title: Wrong refinement horizon in the general spectral construction

failure_location.quote: Given $h_{n_2,j}(z,F)$ for $j=1,\ldots,n_2$, let $k$ be the largest such $j$

issues.failure_explanation: For fixed n2, inspecting only h_{n2,j} with j at most n2 makes the membership decision independent of the inner refinement parameter n1. Consequently, convergence of h_{n2,n1} as n1 tends to infinity cannot imply the two set inclusions claimed for the limiting Gamma_{n2}.
issues.overall_effect: The written construction does not establish the Sigma_2 pseudospectral algorithm for general continuous systems, its Pi_3 spectral consequence, the measure-preserving specialization that reuses it, or the disk upper bound that adapts the same construction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the range j=1,…,n2 by j=1,…,n1 when selecting the latest separated-interval visit. With that correction, Γ_{n2,n1} genuinely refines with n1, and the existing eventual-membership argument supplies the inner limit and the stated inclusions used by thm2 and the disk upper bound.
issues.why_classification: The notation h_{n2,n1}, the definition of Γ_{n2,n1}, and the displayed limit as n1 tends to infinity uniquely force n1 as the refinement horizon. A reader can make this single index correction and follow the existing proof without repairing any mathematical inference or construction.

issues.title: Inconsistent handling of repeated inexact queries in the disk adversary

failure_location.quote: We may also assume that the $\Delta_1$-information consists of distinct points $Y_1=\{y_{1,1},y_{1,2},\ldots,y_{1,N_1}\}$

issues.failure_explanation: Under the old definition, the input contains values f_{j,n}(F) indexed by both source and precision, and an algorithm may query the same source at several precisions or query adaptively chosen sources. The proof's single set Y and subsequent exact substitution for F_1 do not ensure agreement with every queried f_{j,n}; nor is the asserted disjointness of source and returned points automatic when arbitrary points may be sampled. Hence general-algorithm consistency cannot transfer the old output event to F_1 as claimed.
issues.overall_effect: The probabilistic lower bound for measure-preserving disk maps, and the corresponding disk part of the main impossibility theorem, are not established for the old all-point, inexact evaluation interface.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: On each finite-query event, retain the complete list of queried source–precision pairs, group them by source x, and let p(x) be the largest queried precision. Choose the initial inexact data with strict error slack, then choose distinct interpolation targets w_x outside the finite source set and sufficiently close to the corresponding exact perturbed-map values that every previously returned value remains within 2^−n of w_x for each queried (x,n). Apply technical_lemma to the distinct source and target sets, reuse all queried values as admissible inexact data for the conjugated map, extend the unqueried data arbitrarily, and repeat this consistency construction at every nested stage. This preserves the old adaptive all-point interface and restores the disk lower bound and its thm1 consequence.
issues.why_classification: A complete repair is available without changing the theorem or the adversarial conjugacy architecture, but it requires a new finite-query interpolation and precision-bookkeeping argument that handles repeated and adaptively generated sources throughout the induction. This is contained and preserves all guarantees, yet is more than a routine local edit, so it is moderate rather than minor or serious.

issues.title: Uncontrolled reciprocal transition derivative

failure_location.quote: It follows from the bound \cref{deriv_bound}, that $F_{c^{(2)}}\in \Omega_{[0,1]}^{\delta}$.

issues.failure_explanation: At a tail switch, the relevant ratio is q=r_prev(1-r_new)/(1-r_prev), while q^{-1}=r_prev^{-1}(1-r_prev)/(1-r_new). The old condition bounds each factor in the latter product by 1+delta, which gives only a possible (1+delta)^2 bound. For example, delta=0.1, r1=0.91 and r2=0.918 satisfy every displayed old bound, but the reciprocal transition ratio is about 1.206, greater than 1.1. Thus membership in Omega_[0,1]^delta does not follow.
issues.overall_effect: The adversarial maps used for the interval lower bound are not shown to remain in the theorem's input class, so that lower bound and its main-text specialization are unsupported until the construction invariant is repaired.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the local parameter choice so that the actual transition ratios and their reciprocals are bounded by 1+δ. For example, choose r1 sufficiently close to 1 that r1^−2<1+δ, set r2=r1+(1−r1)^2, and then choose τ>0 small enough for the required spectral separation. The tail ratios and both switch directions then obey the derivative bound; retain strict margin when smoothing. The remainder of the alternating-tail construction is unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The defect is genuine, but an elementary local reparameterization and a few direct inequalities restore membership in Ω_[0,1]^δ at every switch while preserving the same annuli, input class, lower bound, and dependent conclusion. No new lemma, proof architecture, or mathematical weakening is required.

issues.title: Invalid decreasing rearrangement in the annulus estimate

failure_location.quote: let $d_1\geq d_2\geq d_3\geq\cdots$ be a reordering of the sequence $\{b_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}$

issues.failure_explanation: A bounded sequence can approach its supremum without attaining it, in which case no first element exists for a non-increasing reordering. The lemma's assumptions allow this behavior for the tail of b_n, so the object d1,d2,... used in the spectral-radius argument is not guaranteed to exist. The resulting spectral containment is therefore not established by the old proof.
issues.overall_effect: The outer spectral-radius bound in the phase-transition lemma is unsupported, and the interval theorem's asserted annular spectra and ensuing main lower bound depend on that bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the nonexistent decreasing rearrangement by a uniform central-tail estimate. Given η>0, choose L so that b_n is at most (1+δ_F)/α+η for |n|>L. Any consecutive block of length l contains at most 2L+1 central terms, whose uniformly bounded contribution divided by l tends to zero; hence the required limsup of the block averages is at most (1+δ_F)/α. Apply the analogous estimate to F^−1 and then continue with Gelfand's formula as written.
issues.why_classification: The old inference is invalid and therefore not a typo, but the missing step is a standard one-paragraph tail estimate. It preserves the lemma's spectral containment and the interval lower-bound chain exactly, with no new construction or substantive loss.

issues.title: Wrong summand index in the RAGE average
issues.failure_explanation: Because the old summand does not depend on k, the factor 2n1+1 cancels and W_{n2,n1}(g) is just one approximation associated with time n1. It need not converge to the Cesaro average of ||P_{n2}K_F^k g||^2 required by thm:RAGE_discrete_time, so the claimed pure-point mass limit does not follow.
issues.overall_effect: The written Sigma_2 upper-bound algorithm for the eigenfunction decision problem, and the corresponding upper-bound part of the main theorem, are not established by the old formula.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the constant summand m_{n2,n1}(g) by m_{n2,k}(g), so that W_{n2,n1}(g) is the Cesàro average of the approximations to ||P_{n2}K_F^k g||² for k=−n1,…,n1. The stated RAGE limit and the upper-bound part of thm4 then follow from the existing argument.
issues.why_classification: The summation variable k, the prior definition of m_{n,ℓ}, and the displayed RAGE theorem uniquely force this correction. The proof already reasons about the Cesàro average, so no mathematical inference or construction needs to be invented.

issues.title: False absence of nonconstant invariant eigenfunctions

failure_location.quote: It follows that there are no eigenfunctions in the subspace $\mathrm{span}\{1\}^\perp$.

issues.failure_explanation: The old lemma claims that strict increase of f on half the torus eliminates every eigenfunction in span{1} perpendicular. But for every nonzero mean-zero h(x), the observable g(x,y)=h(x) lies in that subspace and satisfies K_F g=g because F(x,y) leaves x unchanged. At most, the construction can exclude eigenvalues other than 1; it cannot exclude nonconstant 1-eigenfunctions.
issues.overall_effect: The lower bound for deciding the existence of nonconstant eigenfunctions, and the associated weak-mixing and latent-coordinate claims, are not established. The pure-point eigenvalue-set problem is not refuted by this counterexample because all these invariant functions have eigenvalue 1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: The only source-established complete correction is to replace the decision target by whether K_F has an eigenvalue λ≠1, compute pure-point mass on the unit circle with {1} removed, and revise thm:torus, thm4, and the surrounding prose to withdraw the claims about weak mixing, arbitrary nonconstant eigenfunctions, and invariant latent coordinates. The separate lower bound for the pure-point eigenvalue set may be retained. Preserving the original decision problem instead would require a fundamentally different adversarial family containing a genuinely weak-mixing phase while maintaining all smoothness, measure-preservation, Lipschitz, and finite-data matching requirements.
issues.why_classification: Every old skew product fixes x, so every nonconstant mean-zero h(x) is a 1-eigenfunction; no local proof repair can make the claimed zero phase true. The concrete revised route excludes a natural infinite-dimensional invariant eigenspace and removes the weak-mixing and associated latent-coordinate conclusions, which is major mathematical loss. The only alternative would be essentially new global lower-bound architecture, so no moderate complete route is established.

issues.title: Invalid conjugacy in the torus skew-product lemma

failure_location.quote: For (a), note that the map $F$ is $C^0$ conjugate to $G(x,y)=(x,y+x)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The old f is symmetric, periodic and takes values in [0,pi], so it is not globally one-to-one and has degree zero as a circle map. Consequently F_f is homotopic to the identity on the torus, whereas G(x,y)=(x,y+x) induces a nontrivial shear. Conjugate maps must have conjugate induced winding actions, so the asserted C0 conjugacy cannot hold. No alternative conjugating homeomorphism is supplied.
issues.overall_effect: Independently of the false no-nonconstant-eigenfunction statement, the written proof does not establish the phase with pure-point eigenvalue set {1}, which is used in the pure-point-spectrum lower-bound construction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the false conjugacy claim and prove the needed eigenvalue-set phase directly. Expand g(x,y)=Σ_k g_k(x)e^{iky}; on the kth Fourier mode, K_F acts by multiplication by e^{ikf(x)}. For k≠0, strict monotonicity on each half of the circle makes every level set of e^{ikf(x)} finite and hence null, so no such mode supports an eigenfunction. The k=0 modes give only eigenvalue 1, establishing Sp_pp(K_F)={1}; the plateau argument for the opposite phase remains unchanged. This repair must not be used to assert absence of nonconstant 1-eigenfunctions.
issues.why_classification: The conjugacy is genuinely false, but the pure-point eigenvalue-set conclusion needed by the affected lower-bound chain follows from a short, standard Fourier-mode calculation using only the old hypotheses. This local bypass preserves the relevant theorem and construction without weakening their guarantee or introducing new architecture.
